## Statement

For an aggregate Poisson arm, component ML-NMR multiplies total exposure by the mean modeled rate under the supplied covariate integration distribution. If unweighted participant moments are supplied, that is exact only when exposure has zero covariance with the modeled individual rate; full independence of exposure and covariates is sufficient but not necessary, and treatment-dependent mean follow-up alone is already absorbed by each arm's own total exposure. The problem is within-arm association between exposure and rate-relevant covariates, which is what differential follow-up by prognosis produces, and publications almost never report exposure-weighted covariate summaries. This is a property of the Poisson aggregate likelihood rather than of any one package: multinma also fits Poisson models with a log time-at-risk offset.

## Why it is open

The integration over the aggregate covariate distribution uses reported unweighted moments while the Poisson rate is a person-time-weighted functional of covariates, and sicker patients typically contribute less follow-up, which is exactly the association that breaks the zero-covariance requirement. The correct input, exposure-weighted covariate summaries, is essentially never published, and the current interface neither labels which weighting a supplied moment set represents nor models the weighting itself. There is no diagnostic that tells an analyst whether the omitted covariance is material for their contrast.

## What has been tried

::: {.table-scroll}

| Work | What it contributes |
|---|---|
| [multinma 0.8.0 NEWS, Poisson time-at-risk offset](https://cran.r-project.org/package=multinma) | fits Poisson models with a log time-at-risk offset, so the same exposure-weighting requirement applies outside component models |
| [cpaic 0.1.0 (development version, choxos/cpaic@9d150e9)](https://github.com/choxos/cpaic) | unreleased development R package on GitHub, not on CRAN; computes each aggregate Poisson arm as total exposure times the mean modeled rate over unweighted covariate integration points, with no exposure-weighted moment interface and no joint exposure-covariate model |

:::

## Probable solution or research direction

Label the weighting convention in the interface, so an analyst who can obtain exposure-weighted covariate moments can supply them and make the existing likelihood correct, and request those summaries from data holders as a reporting item. Where only unweighted moments exist, model exposure and covariates jointly so the person-time weighting is generated by the model rather than assumed away. Add a sensitivity calculation for the magnitude of the exposure-rate covariance that would move a target contrast, since the severity is entirely conditional on that quantity.

## Verification

::: {.verification-trail}
**Verdict.** Unverifiable. Auditors disagreed and the disagreement was evidence-bearing on both sides.

**The source titled this.** "Poisson AgD likelihood assumes exposure independent of covariates" The title states independence of exposure and covariates as the required condition, but the audit showed the necessary condition is zero covariance between exposure and the modeled rate.

**The source said.** "The Poisson aggregate-data likelihood in component ML-NMR assumes exposure time is independent of covariates. When exposure depends on prognosis or on treatment, the exposure-weighted covariate moments that actually drive the rate differ from the unweighted moments reported in publications."

**What was wrong with it.** The source stated independence of exposure and covariates as the required condition and framed the issue as package-specific. GPT-5.6 Sol read the Poisson Stan code at choxos/cpaic@9d150e9 and showed the necessary condition is zero covariance between exposure and the modeled rate, not independence, and that supplying exposure-weighted covariate summaries through the existing moment fields makes the same likelihood correct; the literature auditor noted the same requirement applies to multinma's Poisson models, so this is field-level rather than a defect of one implementation.

**Dissent.** codex dissented (overstated): C2 and C3 are supported, but C1 states a sufficient condition as though it were necessary. The AgD Stan likelihood computes total exposure multiplied by the mean modeled rate under the supplied covariate integration distribution. If that distribution represents unweighted participants, exactness requires mean(e_i exp(eta_i)) = mean(e_i) mean(exp(eta_i)), equivalently zero covariance between exposure and the modeled rate. Full independence of exposure and covariates is sufficient but not necessary. Treatment-dependent mean follow-up alone is handled by each arm's own total E; the problem arises from within-arm association between exposure and rate-relevant covariates. Conversely, supplying an exposure-weighted covariate distribution through the existing moment fields can make the same likelihood correct even though the interface does not label or model that weighting. No joint exposure-covariate model is implemented. Severity is high only when the omitted covariance is material.

Literature and prior-art check
:   **open / supported-with-caveat.** The statistical point is correct and non-trivial: a Poisson rate is a person-time-weighted functional of covariates, published covariate moments are person-weighted, and the two coincide only under independence of exposure and covariates, which is exactly what differential follow-up by prognosis violates. I found no paper addressing exposure-weighted covariate moments in an aggregate-data integrated likelihood. Caveat for the editor: this is a field-level property of the Poisson aggregate likelihood, not a cpaic defect. multinma also fits Poisson models with a log time-at-risk offset (its 0.8.0 NEWS records a bug fix to that offset), and the same independence assumption applies there, so framing it as 'cpaic's Poisson aggregate-data likelihood assumes...' understates the reach of the problem. The claim that joint exposure and covariate models are not implemented in cpaic is a code fact I cannot verify from public sources.

GPT-5.6 Sol, technical and source-code lens
:   **open / overstated.** C2 and C3 are supported, but C1 states a sufficient condition as though it were necessary. The AgD Stan likelihood computes total exposure multiplied by the mean modeled rate under the supplied covariate integration distribution. If that distribution represents unweighted participants, exactness requires mean(e_i exp(eta_i)) = mean(e_i) mean(exp(eta_i)), equivalently zero covariance between exposure and the modeled rate. Full independence of exposure and covariates is sufficient but not necessary. Treatment-dependent mean follow-up alone is handled by each arm's own total E; the problem arises from within-arm association between exposure and rate-relevant covariates. Conversely, supplying an exposure-weighted covariate distribution through the existing moment fields can make the same likelihood correct even though the interface does not label or model that weighting. No joint exposure-covariate model is implemented. Severity is high only when the omitted covariance is material.

Grok 4.5, recency lens
:   **open / supported.** cpaic man/cmlnmr.Rd and NEWS state that Poisson aggregate arms use E * mean(exp(eta)) over unweighted covariate integration points and assume exposure independent of covariates; there is no interface for exposure-weighted moments or a joint exposure–covariate model. Literature search for Poisson AgD ML-NMR with person-time depending on covariates did not surface an evaluated method that closes this for component ML-NMR. The statistical claim that exposure-weighted moments differ from unweighted moments under dependence is standard rate epidemiology, not a solved software gap. Queries: Poisson aggregate exposure covariate independent ML-NMR; cpaic poisson exposure; person-time weighted covariate moments NMA. All three claims remain supported; problem open.

Decision path
:   `R5:default-open → R7:counter-and-support-both-present`

:::
